title: CmdPal: App is not being properly disposed
summary: Command Palette invokes asynchronous extension shutdown from MainWindow.Closed and then terminates the process immediately, so services may never finish disposal.

status.label: Design ready - needs approval
status.detail: Move process shutdown ownership to App and await extension disposal before closing the process.

next_action: Approve the lifecycle design to create the fork-side implementation trace.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report and maintainer discussion identify a concrete lifecycle defect; no linked PR implements a coordinated shutdown.

proposed_fixes.title: Coordinate CmdPal shutdown through App
proposed_fixes.root_cause: MainWindow_Closed starts asynchronous extension shutdown and then calls Environment.Exit(0) without awaiting the stop tasks or providing a normal disposal boundary.
plan: Introduce one idempotent App-owned shutdown coordinator in src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/App.xaml.cs that snapshots extension services, awaits their SignalStopAsync tasks, performs cleanup once, and retains forced termination only as the final documented fallback.

Change MainWindow.MainWindow_Closed in src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/MainWindow.xaml.cs to preserve window-position persistence and UI cleanup while delegating lifecycle completion to the App coordinator instead of independently exiting.
Inspect IExtensionService.SignalStopAsync implementations and add focused lifecycle tests for completion, failure handling, and repeated shutdown without assuming an unverified timeout contract.
verification: Build the CmdPal UI project and existing unit-test projects using repository-supported commands.
Close CmdPal through window and external exit paths and confirm extension stop/dispose completion is logged before process termination.
Repeat shutdown and confirm there is no duplicate disposal, unobserved task exception, or tray/keyboard cleanup regression.

confidence.rationale: The unawaited SignalStopAsync calls followed by Environment.Exit are directly confirmed in source and discussion, but the exact service completion and timeout contract still requires implementation-time inspection.

judgment.rationale: The issue points to the exact close handler, and the current source confirms asynchronous SignalStopAsync calls are discarded before Environment.Exit(0).
evidence: Observed: MainWindow_Closed enumerates IExtensionService instances and calls SignalStopAsync without awaiting or observing the returned tasks.
Observed: MainWindow_Closed immediately calls Environment.Exit(0), which bypasses normal managed cleanup.
Observed: App also owns a NativeEventWaiter shutdown callback that disposes ETW, closes AppWindow, and terminates the process.
Observed: the discussion identifies MainWindow as a second lifecycle driver and questions whether the asynchronous signal reaches extensions.
Inferred: services registered in the container can remain undisposed or be interrupted during forced process termination.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a coordinated App-owned shutdown path, retaining the WinUI crash workaround only where required and preserving window-position persistence.

issue_context.summary: CmdPal closes by starting asynchronous extension stop calls from MainWindow.Closed and then forcibly exiting.
known_information: The issue is open and labeled Issue-Bug and Product-Command Palette.
The report identifies MainWindow.xaml.cs and the Environment.Exit call.
A collaborator reports that App starts lifecycle work while MainWindow is also the finish line.
A collaborator notes that asynchronous shutdown calls may not complete before termination.
inferences: Forced termination is the likely reason disposable services do not complete normal cleanup.
A single idempotent shutdown coordinator is safer than adding more cleanup to MainWindow.
issue_context.analysis: The exact disposal contract of every extension is not visible from the issue alone. The source nevertheless establishes an unsafe ordering: fire-and-forget stop signals, then process termination. The design should centralize shutdown and make completion observable without blocking the UI thread indefinitely.
initial_investigation: Read MainWindow_Closed and App constructor shutdown handling in the current PowerToys checkout.
Reviewed recent repository history, including CmdPal lifecycle and JSON-RPC disposal hardening commits.
Reviewed the only timeline cross-reference, which is an unrelated open clipboard-history pull request rather than an existing fix.

information_gaps.why_needed: The final coordinator must avoid hanging shutdown while still allowing normal disposal to complete.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Inspect the service interface and implementations during implementation; add a focused shutdown test for completion and cancellation behavior.

design.root_cause: MainWindow_Closed is acting as an uncoordinated process lifecycle owner. It starts asynchronous extension shutdown, performs local cleanup, and calls Environment.Exit(0) without awaiting extension tasks or giving the DI container a normal disposal boundary.
evidence: Observed in src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/MainWindow.xaml.cs: MainWindow_Closed calls SignalStopAsync for each extension and immediately calls Environment.Exit(0).
Observed in src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/App.xaml.cs: a separate NativeEventWaiter callback also performs shutdown and calls Environment.Exit(0).
Inferred from the collaborator comment: two lifecycle drivers can race and async signals can be lost.

affected_files.purpose: Current close event and window-owned cleanup.
Application startup and external shutdown event.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: External shutdown disposes ETW and closes the window, then terminates the process directly.
implementation_steps.change: Introduce one idempotent App-owned shutdown coordinator that snapshots and awaits extension stop tasks, performs application cleanup once, and only uses forced termination after the existing WinUI workaround is applied.
edge_cases: Do not run cleanup twice when window close and external exit arrive together.
Keep the UI-thread-affine acrylic cleanup on the UI thread.
Surface extension failures through existing logging rather than silently swallowing them.
Define a bounded policy only after inspecting SignalStopAsync implementations.
tests: Add or extend a CmdPal unit test with two fake extension services and assert both stop tasks are awaited once.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The close handler persists settings, fires unawaited extension stops, destroys the tray icon, cleans UI resources, and exits.
implementation_steps.change: Retain position persistence and UI cleanup, but delegate lifecycle completion to the App coordinator and remove the independent forced-exit path.
edge_cases: Preserve tray destruction and keyboard hook disposal ordering.
Do not change normal window-position persistence.
tests: Manual close from the tray and window chrome; verify extension logs show completed disposal before process exit.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The issue does not establish whether all implementations are awaitable, idempotent, or bounded.
implementation_steps.change: Audit implementations and document the completion contract; adapt the coordinator to the actual contract rather than assuming disposal semantics.
edge_cases: A failing extension must not prevent remaining extensions from receiving stop.
Do not introduce a broad catch that hides failures; aggregate or log them using project conventions.
tests: Focused service lifecycle tests for success, failure, and repeated shutdown.

verify: Build the CmdPal UI project and its existing unit-test projects using the repository-supported commands discovered during implementation.
Start CmdPal, load an extension, close through the window and external exit paths, and confirm stop/dispose completion is logged before process termination.
Repeat shutdown twice and confirm no duplicate disposal, unobserved task exception, or tray/keyboard cleanup regression.
risks: Awaiting extension shutdown can delay exit if an implementation never completes.
Changing the close event to async can expose reentrancy or UI-thread affinity issues.
Forced termination may remain necessary for the documented WinUI failure mode, but it must be the final fallback rather than the first cleanup mechanism.
alternatives: Only remove Environment.Exit. Rejected because the application still needs an explicit, coordinated shutdown path.
Keep MainWindow as lifecycle owner and await there. Rejected because App already owns another shutdown path and the issue specifically identifies split ownership.
Dispose every service synchronously from the window. Rejected because extension stop is asynchronous and synchronous blocking risks UI hangs.

notes: The exact service timeout contract remains an implementation discovery item, so the design does not prescribe an unverified timeout.

actions.label: Approve CmdPal lifecycle design

comment.body: The current source confirms that extension stop tasks are started from MainWindow.Closed and the process exits immediately. Please confirm whether any CmdPal extension requires a bounded shutdown timeout or has a known disposal failure, so the App-owned coordinator can preserve cleanup without hanging exit.
